facts.text: Serve dessert when George finally gets to eat something.
facts.why: The plot gives no single moment of George finally eating; the clear food scenes are the dining car with only sandwiches, olives and crackers, and George cracking a tooth on stale Cracker Jacks in Central Park.
facts.fix: Serve dessert when George cracks a tooth on Cracker Jacks.

facts.text: the flight that gets diverted to Boston, and nothing left to eat on board
facts.why: Wikipedia confirms the diversion to Boston and the luggage left behind there, but nothing shows food running out on the plane.
facts.fix: the flight that gets diverted to Boston, with their luggage left behind

facts.text: the only food they find all night
facts.why: This goes with 'Central Park hot dogs'. Hot dogs are not in the plot summary. The food they find is peanut butter sandwiches, olives and crackers on the train, then stale Cracker Jacks in the park that crack George's tooth (the cover photo shows the box).
facts.fix: a snack for George and Gwen in Central Park

facts.text: breakfast in the room at last
facts.why: Their guaranteed reservation is given away and the hotel is full, so they never get a room or a breakfast; George reaches his interview with virtually no food or sleep.

facts.text: rationed between George and Gwen through one very long night
facts.why: No source mentions shortbread or rationing; the food shown is the sandwiches, olives and crackers left in the dining car and the stale Cracker Jacks.
facts.fix: a stand-in for the crackers on the dining car

vibe.verdict: A dry, well dressed Waldorf menu with the Cracker Jacks photo and Gwen's steak note, but the tooth cue and everything going wrong don't print.
